For each possible \(y\), let \(d=y(y-1)(y-2)\). If \(d\mid 14400\), set \(q=14400/d\) and require \(q=x(x-1)\).

Since \(d\le 14400\), we only need \(y\le 25\). Checking \(y=3,\dots,25\), the valid cases are:

\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c|c}
y & d & q & x\\
\hline
4 & 24 & 600 & 25\\
5 & 60 & 240 & 16\\
10 & 720 & 20 & 5
\end{array}
\]

Thus the possible totals \(x+y\) are \(29,21,15\), so the maximum is \(29\).

\[
\boxed{29}
\]
